claims.text: Controlled heat treatments can promote nanoscale chemical short-range order in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
Varying the cooling rate can tune the formation, size, and spatial distribution of CSRO clusters.
The initial as-cast or minimally processed alloy has a largely random elemental distribution and little CSRO.
CSRO clusters moderate the distribution of magnetic exchange energies and produce a more uniform local magnetic environment.
CSRO cluster size and spatial distribution correlate with magnetic-exchange homogeneity.
CSRO cluster size and spatial distribution correlate with reduced local stress fields.
CSRO minimizes domain-wall pinning and thereby lowers coercivity and hysteresis losses.
A more uniform exchange environment produces a well-defined, nearly reversible second-order magnetic transition at low applied fields.
Optimized CSRO increases magnetic entropy change at low applied fields relative to an as-cast or unoptimized baseline.
An optimal cooling rate reduces hysteresis losses relative to the baseline.
Relief of local stress by CSRO enhances heat exchange.
Optimized CSRO maintains rapid heat-transfer performance.
Optimized CSRO maintains or improves mechanical strength and robustness.
Nanoscale coherent particles with low coherency stress can strengthen and improve the ductility of a Fe-Co-Ni-based multicomponent alloy.
The proposed mechanism should apply to compositions similar to FeCoNi-based rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
The mechanism should hold only in a thermal-processing window that encourages CSRO without excessive coarsening or unwanted phase separation.
The mechanism may cease to apply when cluster or particle size significantly exceeds the magnetic domain-wall width.
The exact CSRO size distribution and concentration threshold needed for optimal magnetocaloric performance are unknown.
